query: What recurring issues drive resolution inefficiency?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: A clean categorization of the incident type derived directly from short_description (printer, database, network). Gives a strong grouping axis for finding recurring issue clusters that drive inefficiency. Values are well-grounded in the source text.

per_column.name: failure_mode
per_column.rationale: Orthogonal axis capturing HOW things fail (not_responding, connectivity_failure, physical_damage). Useful for diagnosing recurring failure patterns. Mostly well-read from text; 'not_responding' for vague 'not working properly' is a reasonable inference, and NULL is used appropriately for silent rows.

per_column.name: issue_nature
per_column.rationale: Coarser classification (hardware_failure, software_error) that overlaps substantially with failure_mode and incident_category; values like connectivity_failure/performance_degradation are literally duplicated across columns, reducing its added leverage. Still grounded and provides a higher-level grouping.

per_column.name: requires_physical_intervention
per_column.rationale: A boolean tied to whether on-site work is needed—relevant to resolution effort/inefficiency. Somewhat inferable from category/failure_mode but adds an actionable axis. Groundedness is moderate since it is an inference; the database row labeled False and printer True are reasonable.

per_column.name: recurrence_signal
per_column.rationale: Directly on-topic for the query, but 92% of rows are True and single-line short descriptions provide no evidence that an incident recurs. Marking 'Internet connectivity lost' and generic printer tickets as recurring is a confident assertion the source text does not support, so groundedness is weak and its near-constant distribution limits usefulness.

per_column.name: scope_context
per_column.rationale: Distinguishes individual vs shared vs infrastructure scope, a genuinely useful axis for prioritizing which recurring issues cause the most disruption. Reasonably inferred from category and phrasing (office printer -> shared_office_resource, floor 3 network -> network_infrastructure).

per_column.name: self_resolved_by_assignee
per_column.rationale: Would be relevant to resolution efficiency, but nothing in the short_description or timestamps indicates whether the assignee self-resolved. The True/False labels appear invented (e.g., True for the network row) and are not derivable from the provided source fields.

per_column.name: urgency_signal
per_column.rationale: Useful to relate severity to inefficiency, and there is an existing priority column making it partly redundant. Some labels are defensible from wording (connectivity lost -> immediate_attention), but 'standard' vs 'immediate' is largely an inference not clearly stated in text.

judge.rationale: The added columns provide several genuinely useful, orthogonal grouping axes (incident_category, failure_mode, scope_context) that directly support finding recurring drivers of resolution inefficiency, and these are well-grounded in the short_description text. Weaknesses: issue_nature overlaps heavily with the other categorical columns, and recurrence_signal and self_resolved_by_assignee assert facts (recurrence, who resolved) that single-line ticket text and the provided timestamps do not support, with near-constant skewed distributions—the two clearest hallucination cases. Overall the set is on-topic and mostly grounded but marred by a couple of unsupported inferred booleans.
